issues.legal_issue: Long public religious use can establish a wakf without proof of express dedication, and property used as an integrated religious unit or incorporated into the endowment by its manager may become part of the wakf.
material_facts: The old mosque had long been used for worship and was already accepted as wakf property, although there was no proof of express dedication.
Later additions were made by persons who claimed to manage the mosque. Worshippers used the demarcated mosque area, including its courtyard and certain extensions, for religious purposes.
A room originally separate from the mosque was opened into it and thereafter used for worship with the mosque.
Buildings on a strip behind and west of the mosque rested on the mosque wall, used it as their back wall, and occupied space that had formed part of the mosque estate.
A urinal, water pipe and bathroom were constructed for worshippers’ use.

Other properties, including the Imambara, tombs, eastern shops and certain separately severable plots, were claimed and dealt with as private property; public religious use of them was absent, insubstantial or not established.
issues.conclusion: The old mosque, the qualifying integrated and religiously used additions, the buildings on the western strip that incorporated mosque land, and the worshipper amenities were wakf property. The remaining disputed properties were not shown to be wakf or accretions to the wakf.
issues.legal_principle: A wakf normally requires express dedication, but where land has been used from time immemorial for a religious purpose it may be wakf by user despite the absence of evidence of express dedication (as stated in Mulla’s Mahomedan Law). The court treated a separately demarcated compact area used as one unit for worship as a single wakf unit, and treated qualifying additions and amenities as part of the endowment. Mere proximity, occasional use, passage to a mosque, or use not shown to be for religious purposes did not establish dedication.

rule.if: wakf_status_claim and (long_public_religious_use or (manager_added_property and (integrated_with_endowment or used_as_worship_amenity)))

predicates.wakf_status_claim: A claimant seeks recognition of disputed property as part of a religious endowment.
predicates.long_public_religious_use: The public has used the property for a religious purpose over a very long period.
predicates.manager_added_property: A person acting as manager of the endowment added or constructed the disputed property.
predicates.integrated_with_endowment: The added property was physically incorporated into the endowment property or formed part of a compact unit used for worship.
predicates.used_as_worship_amenity: The property was constructed or used as an amenity for people attending worship.

issues.definition: When a religious-endowment claim concerns property with long public religious use, or property added by its manager and integrated with the endowment or used as a worship amenity, the qualifying property is treated as wakf.

issues.legal_issue: A manager of a religious endowment cannot claim as personal property a structure built by integrating endowment land into a composite structure.
material_facts: The managers claimed to act as mutwallis of the mosque.
Buildings they constructed behind and west of the mosque rested on its wall and incorporated parts of the mosque estate into composite rooms.
A formerly separate room was opened into the mosque and became an integral part of it.
The managers also asserted personal claims over some of these properties.
issues.conclusion: The managers could not assert a personal title adverse to the wakf over the integrated structures; the relevant structures were treated as accretions to the wakf estate.
issues.legal_principle: A trustee or manager cannot set up a title hostile to the trust or obtain a personal benefit from trust property. Where a manager builds on trust land so that the part on that land and the remaining structure form one integrated unit, the structure is treated as an accretion to the trust estate, and the manager is estopped from claiming it personally.

predicates.wakf_trust_case: The dispute concerns property held or claimed as part of a religious endowment.
predicates.manager_claimed_trustee_capacity: The person who constructed or controlled the property claimed to act as manager or trustee of the endowment.
predicates.manager_built_integrated_structure_on_en: The manager built a structure that incorporated endowment land into a physically integrated unit.

issues.definition: If a manager acting in that capacity builds an integrated structure incorporating endowment land, the manager cannot claim the integrated structure personally.

issues.legal_issue: The limitation bar does not apply to a claim concerning property comprised in a religious endowment held in trust for a specific purpose.
material_facts: The defendant argued that the claim was barred by the six-year period under Article 120 of the Limitation Act because the cause of action had arisen long before the suit.
The court found that parts of the disputed property were comprised in the wakf estate.

The proviso to Section 10 of the Limitation Act deemed property comprised in a Muhammadan religious or charitable endowment to be vested in trust for a specific purpose and its manager to be the trustee.
issues.conclusion: No question of limitation arose for the parts of the disputed property found to be comprised in the wakf estate.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 10 and its proviso of the Limitation Act, property comprised in a Muhammadan religious or charitable endowment is deemed to be property vested in trust for a specific purpose, and its manager is deemed to be its trustee. The court therefore held that limitation did not bar the claim in respect of property comprised in the wakf estate.

predicates.limitation_defense_in_endowment_property: A defendant relies on lapse of time to resist a claim concerning property claimed as part of an endowment.
predicates.property_is_comprised_in_religious_endow: The property is found to be comprised in a religious endowment held in trust for a specific purpose.

issues.definition: When a limitation defense is raised against a claim concerning property comprised in a religious endowment, the claim is not barred by limitation.

issues.legal_issue: Worshippers have an easementary right of way over the only access route to reach a mosque and its worship-related facilities.
material_facts: Worshippers used a plot to reach the mosque and the urinal, water tap and bathroom.
The evidence and map showed that there was no other access to the mosque across that plot.
The court found that the worshippers’ use of the plot for passage did not itself establish that the plot had been dedicated as wakf.
issues.conclusion: The worshippers had an easementary right of way over the plot for ingress to and egress from the mosque and its precincts, and for access to the urinal, water tap and bathroom.
issues.legal_principle: The court recognized an easementary right of way on the facts that worshippers needed to cross the plot to reach the mosque and related facilities and that no other access was available. Passage over the plot did not, by itself, establish that the plot was wakf property.

predicates.mosque_access_dispute: The dispute concerns a route used to reach a mosque or its related facilities.
predicates.worshippers_use_route_to_reach_mosque_or: Worshippers cross the route to reach the mosque or facilities used in connection with worship.
predicates.no_alternative_access: There is no other available route for that access.

issues.definition: Where worshippers use a route to reach a mosque or its facilities and no alternative access exists, they have an easementary right of way over that route.
